Subject: Initial sizing ask for EdgeSight private pool

Hey Vivek —

Thanks for taking this on. Quick summary of what we need from Redwood to finish our procurement plan:

- Sustained inference throughput target: ~2,000 tokens/sec (mixed prompt lengths) for baseline production.
- Burst capacity: up to ~8,000 tokens/sec for short windows (~3-5 minutes) during peak ML pipeline runs.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn short generation (<= 64 tokens).
- QoS: ability to reserve capacity for critical routes, and an admission policy to avoid noisy-tenant impact.

Attached is our current network diagram and a very rough traffic histogram. Also: we need an early estimate of how many GPUs, NIC sizing, and whether we should plan for 2x regional failover or local redundancy only.

Can you and your team propose a sizing baseline + a short rationale (batching assumptions, KV cache warmup, expected amortized tokens/sec per GPU) so we can map to our budget and timeline?

We'd like a short call the week of Oct 25 to walk through tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Sanjay
Head of Platform, EdgeSight Labs

Sanjay — thanks for the clear brief and the diagram. I've sketched a baseline and attached a small capacity model (capacity-model-v2.xlsx) plus a simplified topology PNG. High-level findings below; happy to walk through on a call.

Baseline assumptions we used
- Model: 70B decoder with KV cache (quantized to int8-ish profile) – representative of the family you described.
- Workload mix: 60% short chat-like (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64–512), 10% long (>512).
- Effective batching: continuous batching target ~20–30 tokens per batch at 100ms max queueing for short requests.
- KV cache hit rate: warm pool assumptions assume 70% cache hits for repeated prefixes after 10–15 min warm-up.

Sizing summary (initial)
- Per-GPU steady-state throughput (baseline config): ~300–400 tokens/sec for short-turn dominated mixes at p95 120–160ms depending on batching.
- Burst headroom: with autoscale buffer and cold-start amortization, plan ~35% headroom beyond steady-state.
- Recommended starting footprint: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA H100/A100-class equivalent) in a local private pool to meet sustained 2k tokens/sec with ~35% headroom.
- For your 8k tokens/sec burst target: recommend burst tiers (hot pool + ephemeral workers) — you will need an additional ~12–16 GPUs spun up within 60–90s depending on model warmup strategy and warm-cache reuse.

Networking & NIC guidance
- NIC per host: plan 100Gbps per host with 1.2x oversubscription limit on the aggregation switch to keep egress spikes bounded.
- Egress shaping: apply per-tenant policing on your leaf switches and use flow-based admission to avoid cross-tenant interference.

Tradeoffs and notes
- Multiplexing more tenants onto fewer GPUs reduces total GPU count but increases p95 tails and complicates admission control.
- Aggressive quantization can drop token latency slightly but requires validation for quality regressions.

Attachments: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), net-topology-diagram.png (image/png)

Proposed next steps
1) Quick 30-min call Wed Oct 27 to go over the spreadsheet and confirm burst policy (we can do 10:00 PT)
2) We provide a short mutual action plan (MAP) mapping GPU counts to SLA tiers and estimated costs
3) If you want regional failover (cold standby), add ~25-30% to GPU baseline for a hot/cold copy and cross-region sync plan.

Let me know if Wed 10:00 PT works.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Vivek — quick note after looking at the sheet:

- If EdgeSight accepts a slightly higher p95 (180–200ms) we can reduce the steady-state GPU count by ~15% using heavier batching for short ops. That assumes clients tolerate 80–120ms average queueing.
- Alternatively, a multiplexed slab where we co-locate multiple tenants and use strict admission/priority lanes could shave GPUs but will require robust telemetry (per-conversation QoS) and likely extra engineering on your side.

Also: for bursts, I prefer the ephemeral worker pattern (spin up ephemeral pods on reserved hosts) vs fully adding permanent GPUs to capacity — faster economics and simpler warm-cache reuse if you pin datasets.

Sanjay / team — thanks for the patience while we assembled the numbers. Short MAP and next steps below.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — high level
- Phase 1 (pilot, 2–4 weeks): deploy 8 GPUs in your private VPC, 100Gbps NIC hosts, admission policy configured for critical routes. Verify steady-state 2k tokens/sec across representative traffic (we'll run our internal probe harness).
- Phase 2 (burst validation, 2 weeks): test ephemeral worker spin-up path to reach ~8k tokens/sec for 3–5 min windows. Measure warm-cache reuse and end-to-end p95.
- Phase 3 (production roll): after validating bursts and telemetry, finalize sizing and add optional cold standby (regional) if you want 2-region resilience (~+25% GPUs).

Deliverables & owners
- Redwood: capacity model workbook + test harness (Vivek / Karthik) — due Oct 30
- EdgeSight: final approval of burst window SLA and network ACLs (Sanjay) — due Nov 3
- Joint call: Wed Oct 27 10:00 PT (confirming calendar) — agenda: walk sheet, agree burst mechanics, sign MAP
